cues.text: Here is a realistic, disciplined trading plan.
cues.say: Here is a realistic, disciplined trading plan.

cues.text: A $100,000 balance. Three trades a day, three days a week. One percent risk on each.
cues.say: A one hundred thousand dollar balance. Three trades a day, three days a week. One percent risk on each.

cues.text: Each trade risks $1,000. That is the stop loss.
cues.say: Each trade risks one thousand dollars. That is the stop loss.

cues.text: The target is 3 percent: $3,000. A risk-to-reward of one to three.
cues.say: The target is three percent. Three thousand dollars. A risk to reward of one to three.

cues.text: And once a trade moves into profit, the stop loss moves to break-even.
cues.say: And once a trade moves into profit, the stop loss moves to break-even.

cues.text: Watch one trade. Entry here. Stop loss below. Target three times further above.
cues.say: Watch one trade. Entry here. Stop loss below. Target three times further above.

cues.text: The price moves up, into profit. Now the stop loss moves up to the entry price.
cues.say: The price moves up, into profit. Now the stop loss moves up to the entry price.

cues.text: From here, the trade cannot lose. If the price turns back, it closes at zero.
cues.say: From here, the trade cannot lose. If the price turns back, it closes at zero.

cues.text: If it keeps going, it hits the target: plus $3,000.
cues.say: If it keeps going, it hits the target. Plus three thousand dollars.

cues.text: A realistic day. One trade hits the target: plus $3,000.
cues.say: A realistic day. One trade hits the target. Plus three thousand.

cues.text: One returns to break-even: zero.
cues.say: One returns to break-even. Zero.

cues.text: One hits the stop loss: minus $1,000.
cues.say: One hits the stop loss. Minus one thousand.

cues.text: The day: plus $2,000. Two percent.
cues.say: The day: plus two thousand dollars. Two percent.

cues.text: At one to three, you break even winning just one trade in four.
cues.say: At one to three, you break even winning just one trade in four.

cues.text: Even the worst day, three losses, costs $3,000. Three percent of the account.
cues.say: Even the worst day, three losses, costs three thousand dollars. Three percent of the account.

cues.text: Three days a week is about 13 trading days a month.
cues.say: Three days a week is about thirteen trading days a month.

cues.text: If the average day matched the example: $26,000 a month,
cues.say: If the average day matched the example: twenty-six thousand dollars a month,

cues.text: and about $256,000 after six months.
cues.say: and about two hundred and fifty-six thousand after six months.

cues.text: Now withdraw 3 percent of the balance every month.
cues.say: Now withdraw three percent of the balance every month.

cues.text: Your initial $100,000 is fully withdrawn by month 14, while the account keeps growing.
cues.say: Your initial one hundred thousand is fully withdrawn by month fourteen, while the account keeps growing.

cues.text: These are projections from one example day, not results.
cues.say: These are projections from one example day, not results.
